newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Common Fund mulls project to widen nickel use.
newsitem.headline: Common Fund mulls project to widen nickel use.

text.p: The Common Fund for Commodities, a U.N. affiliate, said on Monday representatives from two industry bodies had presented it with proposals for a project to designed to broaden use of nickel in the developing world.

A delegation from the International Nickel Study Group and the Nickel Development Institute, led by INSG Secretary-General Glen Wittur, recently visited the Fund's headquarters in Amsterdam to put forward the proposal.
"The proposal centres on the possibility of making people aware of the uses of nickel, mainly in developing countries," the Fund's managing director Rolf Boenker told Reuters.
But he added further work on the proposal was needed and that a decision on whether to proceed could not be expected for a couple of months.

A statement issued by the Fund quoted Wittur as saying, "Although a sizeable percentage of nickel mining takes place in industrial countries, a number of substantive nickel producers are developing dountries and nickel plays an important role in their economies.
"Countries with known but not yet developed nickel resources are Burundi, Ivory Coast, Guatamala, India, Malaysia, Papua New Guinea, Tanzania, Venezuela, Zaire and Zambia."
